course.title: The Youth Impact Training Programme (YITP) — 9-Week Virtual Training
course.description: The Youth Impact Training Programme (YITP) is a comprehensive 9-week virtual training designed to equip young people with essential life skills, career readiness, and entrepreneurial knowledge. Our mission is to empower youth with practical skills and a success-driven mindset to help them excel in both employment and business. 📌 Additional Benefits - Networking & Mentorship Sessions - Professional Certification - 100% Virtual & Flexible Learning - Industry Expert Instructors 🎯 Who Can Join? - High School Students (15+ years) - College & University Students - Graduates & Young Professionals - Job Seekers & Employees
course.learning_objectives: Equip learners with practical life skills, career readiness, and foundational entrepreneurship knowledge; develop a success-driven mindset; and prepare participants to apply skills in both employment and business contexts.

modules.title: Module 1 — UPL 101 Full Module
modules.description: A complete module combining UPL 101 content (foundations, definiteness of purpose, service, and purpose-in-action) into one coherent learning path.

lessons.title: Story of the Three Builders: Purpose & Meaning
lessons.content:
The Story of the Three Builders

Based on the rebuilding of St. Paul’s Cathedral (1666). Three bricklayers respond differently to the same task—earning money, building a strong wall, building a cathedral where people gather and pray. The lesson: Everything is an inside job. How we interpret action flows from purpose and mindset.
lessons.learning_objectives: Retell the bricklayers story and extract its purpose lens (‘inside job’).

lessons.title: Seven Questions for Purpose Clarity (Part A)
lessons.content:
Seven Questions for Clarity (1–4)

  1. What makes you feel most alive?
  2. What problem in the world gets you most emotionally charged?
  3. What are you naturally good at?
  4. What is your life’s most meaningful event or experience?

Journaling prompts accompany each question.
lessons.learning_objectives: Apply questions 1–4 to personal reflection; capture 3–5 insights.

lessons.title: Seven Questions for Purpose Clarity (Part B)
lessons.content:
Seven Questions for Clarity (5–7)

  1. What would you do if you had zero fear?
  2. Who is your idol, living or dead, and why?
  3. What do you want to be your enduring legacy?
lessons.learning_objectives: Apply questions 5–7; draft 3–5 sentence personal insights.

lessons.title: Purpose vs. Vision vs. Goals
lessons.content:
Definitions & Flow

  • Purpose: reason for being.
  • Vision: anticipated future; direction for outcomes.
  • Goals: specific, desired outcomes guiding action.

Sequence: Purpose → Vision → Goals.
lessons.learning_objectives: Differentiate purpose, vision, and goals; explain sequencing.

lessons.title: Purpose-Driven Lives: Gandhi
lessons.content:
Gandhi: Non-violence & Integrity

Gandhi emphasized living, thinking, and acting rightly; non-violent resistance; and liberation.

“The main purpose of life is to live rightly, think rightly, act rightly. The soul must languish when we give all our thought to the body.”
lessons.learning_objectives: Identify Gandhi’s purpose and one behavior to emulate this week.

lessons.title: Purpose-Driven Lives: Mandela & Mother Teresa
lessons.content:
Mandela & Mother Teresa

Mandela: justice, unity, courage, forgiveness; Mother Teresa: compassion, doing small things with great love.

“For to be free is not merely to cast off one’s chains, but to live in a way that respects and enhances the freedom of others.” — Nelson Mandela
lessons.learning_objectives: Describe how resilience and compassion express purpose; select one behavior to practice.

lessons.title: The Baobab—‘Tree of Life’: Service Orientation
lessons.content:
The Baobab Tree

A legendary ‘tree of life’ sustaining communities via fruit, water storage, shelter; a metaphor that true purpose sustains others and serves the community.
lessons.learning_objectives: Explain the Baobab metaphor and connect it to service as purpose.

lessons.title: Major vs. Minor Purposes
lessons.content: You have a major (life) purpose and minor purposes that should feed into the major purpose.
lessons.learning_objectives: Distinguish major and minor purposes; align examples accordingly.

lessons.title: Reflection Journal — ‘When did I feel most alive?’
lessons.content: Guided journaling: capture meaningful experiences; identify themes across moments of aliveness and fulfillment.
lessons.learning_objectives: Journal to surface themes pointing to personal purpose.

lessons.title: Definiteness of Purpose — Overview
lessons.content:
Definiteness of Purpose

‘Get clear, get hungry, get moving, stay locked in.’ Napoleon Hill: ‘Definiteness of purpose is the starting point of all achievement.’
lessons.learning_objectives: Define and justify definiteness of purpose as driver of achievement.

lessons.title: From Vision to Daily Calendar — Consistent Action
lessons.content: Create a flexible plan; convert purpose into daily micro-actions; track progress in calendar.
lessons.learning_objectives: Draft 3 micro-actions aligned to definite purpose and schedule them.

lessons.title: Wheel of Life — Seven Spokes (Part A)
lessons.content: Rate Career, Financial, Spiritual; identify one improvement for each.
lessons.learning_objectives: Assess three domains and propose one improvement each.

lessons.title: Wheel of Life — Seven Spokes (Part B)
lessons.content: Rate Physical, Intellectual, Family, Social; set one habit per domain.
lessons.learning_objectives: Assess four domains and set one habit per domain.

lessons.title: Og Mandino’s Habits (Part A)
lessons.content: Begin with gratitude; greet the day with love; persist until you succeed; live each day as if it is your last.
lessons.learning_objectives: Explain first four habits and propose daily cues.

lessons.title: Og Mandino’s Habits (Part B)
lessons.content: Master emotions; multiply your value; take action now.
lessons.learning_objectives: Plan one ‘act now’ behavior for tomorrow morning.

lessons.title: ‘Send the Elevator Back Down’ — Service as Legacy
lessons.content: Mentoring and multiplying impact: success becomes legacy when you lift others as you rise.
lessons.learning_objectives: Explain the proverb and identify one mentee to support this month.

lessons.title: Mother Teresa — Small Acts, Great Love
lessons.content: Start where you are; see people, not problems; love through action; do small things well; keep your heart soft.
lessons.learning_objectives: Identify 3 actionable small acts to perform this week.

lessons.title: Mandela — Unity, Justice, Forgiveness
lessons.content: Choose unity; stand for justice; forgive to create the future; lead by example; see the bigger picture.
lessons.learning_objectives: Translate one leadership principle into a behavior this week.

lessons.title: Humility & Selflessness — Five Practices
lessons.content: Put mission above ego; listen; share the stage; serve unconditionally; stay grounded.
lessons.learning_objectives: Explain five practices and choose one to apply today.

lessons.title: Folktale — The Tortoise and the Heavy Load
lessons.content: Steady progress despite obstacles; take one micro-step at a time.
lessons.learning_objectives: Name one ‘heavy load’ and one micro-step forward.

lessons.title: Fear vs. Faith; Courage; Inner Clarity
lessons.content: Contrast fear and faith; rehearse courage; write a visualization script for breaking a barrier.
lessons.learning_objectives: Draft a personal visualization script for overcoming an obstacle.

lessons.title: Drafting Your Purpose Statement (Part A)
lessons.content: Align passions, strengths, and values; Success Afrika techniques for clarity.
lessons.learning_objectives: Produce a first-draft purpose statement (3–5 sentences).

lessons.title: Drafting Your Purpose Statement (Part B) — Peer Review
lessons.content: Refine the draft using a peer feedback checklist; iterate to sharpen clarity and alignment.
lessons.learning_objectives: Refine purpose statement via peer feedback.

lessons.title: Purpose into Schedule — Weekly Planner
lessons.content: Convert purpose to time blocks; habits and time-management insights for sustainable action.
lessons.learning_objectives: Create a weekly schedule aligned with purpose.

lessons.title: Proverb — The Child & the Village
lessons.content: ‘The child who is not embraced by the village will burn it down to feel its warmth.’ Purpose thrives in connection and contribution.
lessons.learning_objectives: Explain the proverb and propose one way to build belonging.

lessons.title: Anecdote — The Clay Lamp: Sharing Your Light
lessons.content: A small lamp lights many others without losing its flame — sharing purpose multiplies it.
lessons.learning_objectives: Identify one way to ‘light others’ this week.

lessons.title: Community Project Mini-Design
lessons.content: Draft a small community project aligned to purpose: need, beneficiaries, activities, timeline, and metrics.
lessons.learning_objectives: Produce a one-page mini-proposal for a community project.

lessons.title: River & Stone — Persistence and One-Year Plan
lessons.content: Water shapes rock over time; build a 12-month action plan with milestones and review cadence.
lessons.learning_objectives: Draft a 12-month action plan with quarterly milestones.

quizzes.description: Knowledge check on the ‘inside job’ lens and purpose framing.
quizzes.instructions: Choose the best answer. Read explanations after each item.

quizzes.title: Purpose vs Vision vs Goals
quizzes.description: Check understanding of definitions and sequencing.
quizzes.instructions: Match terms and select correct statements.

quizzes.title: Definiteness of Purpose
quizzes.description: Key ideas from Napoleon Hill and daily focus.

quizzes.title: Fear vs Faith & Courage
quizzes.description: Contrast key terms and visualize breakthrough.

questions.question_text: In the ‘Three Builders’ story, what best explains the third bricklayer’s response?
options: He understood the larger purpose of his work
questions.correct_answer: He understood the larger purpose of his work
questions.explanation: The third bricklayer connected his task to a cathedral, showing a purpose-driven mindset (‘inside job’).

questions.question_text: True or False: Purpose and mindset shape how we interpret our daily actions.
questions.explanation: The lesson emphasizes that interpretation flows from purpose and mindset.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: ‘Everything is an ____ job.’
Match each term to the best description.
questions.explanation: Purpose → Vision → Goals sequence and definitions.

questions.question_text: True or False: Goals give rise to purpose.
questions.explanation: Purpose begets vision; vision begets goals, not the other way around.

questions.question_text: According to Napoleon Hill, what is ‘the starting point of all achievement’?
questions.explanation: This direct quotation anchors the lesson.

questions.question_text: Short Answer: List two elements of the ‘get clear, get hungry, get moving, stay locked in’ framework.
questions.correct_answer: Any two of: get clear; get hungry; get moving; stay locked in.
questions.explanation: Learners should recall at least two elements; partial credit per rubric.

questions.question_text: Which statement best contrasts fear and faith?
options: Fear and faith are identical emotional states
Fear focuses on what can go wrong; faith focuses on what can be made right
questions.correct_answer: Fear focuses on what can go wrong; faith focuses on what can be made right
questions.explanation: The lesson contrasts orientation and focus, not denial of reality.

questions.question_text: Short Answer: Describe one courageous action you will take this week.
questions.correct_answer: Free response aligned to lesson content.

questions.question_text: True or False: Persistence works like water shaping rock over time.
questions.explanation: This is the lesson’s core allegory.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: A one-year plan should include quarterly ______.

assignments.title: Reflection Paper — When did I feel most alive?
assignments.description: Reflective journaling on meaningful experiences and themes.
assignments.instructions: Write 400–600 words connecting your experiences to the Seven Questions for Clarity.

assignments.title: Personal Balance Snapshot
assignments.description: Submit Wheel of Life scores and a 7-day micro-habit plan across seven domains.
assignments.instructions: Attach your scores (0–10) and a table of daily actions for the next 7 days.

assignments.title: Mentor-a-Peer Micro-Service
assignments.description: Plan and execute one act of service/mentoring; document impact.

assignments.title: Purpose Statement (Revised)
assignments.description: Upload a refined purpose statement after peer feedback.
assignments.instructions: Provide a 3–5 sentence statement and a brief rationale (100–150 words).

assignments.title: Community Project Mini-Design
assignments.description: Design a small project aligned to purpose with need, beneficiaries, activities, and metrics.
assignments.instructions: Submit a 1-page proposal (max 500 words) with timeline and success criteria.

assignments.title: One-Year Action Plan
assignments.description: Create a 12-month action plan with quarterly milestones and review cadence.
assignments.instructions: Upload plan (table or document) including milestones, habits, and support network.
